command.journal.syncSuperProductivityJou: Sync All Entries with Super Productivity
Link tasks of the journal to tasks in [Super Productivity](https://super-productivity.com) by their key (`#acme:12`, `:7`): open tasks get the code action *Send to Super Productivity*, completing, reopening or planning a linked task for another day does the same there, **Journal: Sync Tasks with Super Productivity** sends the open tasks of the current page (of a plan: the items without sub-items), imports the tasks planned there for the day and syncs completed, reopened and moved tasks, and **Journal: Sync All Entries with Super Productivity** syncs the linked tasks of the whole journal. The links are kept in `.vscode/superproductivity.json` in the journal. Needs the desktop app with its Local REST API turned on and its token (**Journal: Set Super Productivity API Token**).
Address of the Local REST API of Super Productivity. The API token is sent to this address.

Scopes whose project in Super Productivity has a different title: the slug of the scope and the title or id of the project. A scope named like a project (case ignored) needs no entry. Tasks of a scope are sent to its project, the others to the inbox. Example: `{ "acme": "ACME Relaunch" }`.

configuration.title: VSCode Journal
configuration.journal.base.description: The base directory for your notes. Defaults to the directory 'Journal' in your home directory. Supports embedded variables as described in the Guide.
configuration.journal.ext.description: The default extension of your notes and journal entries. Defaults to markdown (.md).
configuration.journal.locale.description: The locale to use (required for the date format). Defaults to the language setting from Visual Studio Code.
configuration.journal.syntax-highlightin: Enable extension specific syntax highlighting (default is false).
configuration.journal.patternHistory.des: Earlier values of `#journal.patterns#` (and `#journal.ext#`), newest first. When you change the patterns, add the old ones here: entries, weekly entries and notes are then still found where they were written, and new files go to the current patterns. Example: `[{ "until": "2026-10-20", "patterns": { "entries": { "path": "${base}/${year}/${month}", "file": "${day}.${ext}" } } }]`. Copy the old value exactly; it is read as it was while current. See [Changing the layout](https://github.com/pajoma/vscode-journal/blob/develop/docs/settings.md#changing-the-layout).
configuration.journal.patternHistory.unt: The day these patterns were replaced (YYYY-MM-DD). For your reference only.
configuration.journal.patternHistory.pat: The patterns as they were set in `journal.patterns`; unset ones are the defaults.
configuration.journal.patternHistory.ext: The file extension then, if it was not the current `journal.ext`.
configuration.journal.patterns.descripti: Individual patterns which define where and how notes and entries are stored. Check the wiki for defaults and options.
configuration.journal.entryGranularity.d: Whether memos, tasks, and new notes default to today's daily entry (`daily`) or the current week's weekly entry (`weekly`) when no explicit date target is given. Explicit input (date offset, ISO date, weekday, week number) always overrides this setting. Default: `daily`.
configuration.journal.dev.description: If enabled, the features in development will be activated (other features might be broken).
configuration.journal.navigation.mode.de: How `Open Previous` and `Open Next` step through journal entries. `existing` skips gaps and only opens entries that already exist on disk. `calendar` steps exactly one day at a time and creates the entry if missing. Default: `existing`.
configuration.journal.issueLinks.descrip: Turns issue references in journal files into links (Ctrl+click in the editor, links in the markdown preview): a prefix and the URL of its issues, `${id}` is the number. `pida#23` links issue 23 of the prefix `pida`; a prefix that ends with `-` is followed directly by the number (`XX-1234`). Prefixes match in any case; code and URLs are not linked. Only `http` and `https` URLs are used; in untrusted workspaces only the user setting applies. Example: `{ "pida": "https://github.com/owner/pida/issues/${id}", "XX-": "https://jira.example.com/browse/XX-${id}" }`.
configuration.journal.notes.ignore.descr: Files in a notes folder that are not linked from the journal entry, as file name patterns: `*` matches any characters, `?` one character, case is ignored. Example: `["*.png", "*.tmp"]`. Hidden files (`.`), temporary files (`~`) and subfolders are never linked.
configuration.journal.openInNewEditorGro: If true, the journal pages and new notes will split the editor view.
configuration.journal.mcp.enabled.descri: Start the journal MCP server, so AI assistants can read and write your journal: GitHub Copilot finds it without setup, other assistants are set up with the command **Journal: Set up MCP Server**. When off, the server does not start, also for assistants set up before. User settings only.
configuration.journal.scopes.description: Scopes whose folder is not directly below `#journal.scopeRoot#` (written by **Journal: Create Scope**), and templates of scopes. Every folder below `#journal.scopeRoot#` is a scope as well; an entry here with the same name adds its templates. See the [scopes guide](https://github.com/pajoma/vscode-journal/blob/develop/docs/scopes.md).
configuration.journal.scopeRoot.descript: Folder whose sub-folders are scopes. A note titled `#name Title` is stored in the folder `name`. Relative paths are relative to `#journal.base#`. Supported variables: `${base}`, `${homeDir}`, `${workspaceRoot}`, `${workspaceFolder}`.
configuration.journal.scopes.name.descri: Slug of the scope: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter (e.g. `acme` for `#acme`).
configuration.journal.scopes.base.descri: Folder of the scope, inside the journal; relative paths and `${base}` are relative to `#journal.base#`. Without it, the folder is `<scopeRoot>/<name>`.
configuration.journal.scopes.patternHist: No longer read: the notes of a scope are flat in its folder.
configuration.journal.scopes.patterns.de: No longer read: the notes of a scope are flat in its folder.
configuration.journal.scopes.templates.d: Templates of the scope (same format as journal.templates); take precedence over journal.templates.
configuration.journal.templates.descript: Definition of templates used when generate content for the journal. See Guide for more details.
configuration.journal.weeklySync.descrip: Controls the automatic sync of daily-entry links into the weekly file. When enabled, opening a weekly entry (or creating/deleting a daily entry while a weekly file is active) updates the list of links under the configured anchor heading. Set `enabled` to false to disable the feature entirely.
configuration.journal.weeklyTemplateDate: Resolve date variables in the weekly template, counted from the first day of the week (Monday or Sunday, depending on `journal.locale`): `${d:format}`, `${localDate}`, `${weekday}`, `${month}`, `${day}`, and `${d+1:format}` … `${d+6:format}` for the following days. `${year}` is the year the week belongs to. Off by default: then only `${week}` is resolved, as before.
configuration.journal.search.enabled.des: The journal search: the row `Search journal` in the smart input, the command `Journal: Search Journal` and its index. Off: no search, and the journal is not read for it.
configuration.journal.search.indexOnStar: When the search index is built. `local`: in the background a few seconds after VS Code starts, except in remote sessions (SSH, WSL, containers). `always`: also in remote sessions. `never`: when the search opens for the first time.
After startup, not in remote sessions
After startup, also in remote sessions
When the search opens for the first time
configuration.journal.search.content.des: Search the text of entries and notes, not only their titles. Off: the files are not read, and the search uses less memory.
configuration.journal.search.recency.des: How much newer entries and notes are preferred among similar matches: `off` ranks by relevance only, `high` strongly prefers recent files. The date is the day a file belongs to, not its modification date.
The maximum number of search results.
